newsitem.title: JAPAN: Britain not committed yet on joining EMU - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Britain not committed yet on joining EMU - Clarke.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Thursday that Britain has not yet committed itself to joining a single European currency, a Finance Ministry official told reporters.
Clarke also told Mitsuzuka that Britain is likely to meet the criteria for joining the European Monetary Union, a MOF official said.
Britain's economic conditions are very good and its growth rate is among the highest in Europe, with the inflation rate at low levels, Clarke was quoted as saying in their meeting.

Mitsuzuka explained to Clarke that Japan's economic recovery is likely be gradual in the first half of the fiscal year starting April 1997, but is expected to achieve a sustainable recovery centering on private-sector demand in the latter half, the ministry official said.

Mitsuzuka also said Japan is making efforts to achieve fiscal consolidation and would like to meet the cabinet's target of reducing its fiscal deficit to below three percent of its gross domestic product earlier than the original goal of by 2005, the official said.

Mitsuzuka said it was necessary to implement a consumption tax hike to five percent in April from the current three percent and terminate special income tax cuts from this year, in order to achieve fiscal consolidation, the official said.

Clarke told his counterpart that Britain had carried out the privatisation of its nationally owned firms to reduce outstanding public bonds and interest payments and urged Japan to do more in this area, the ministry official said.
Mitsuzuka responded by saying that Japan plans to do so, the official said.
